#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# TESTS for Blockchain/Testing/jobs/04-container-trivy.sh — the image filter
# (KS-867)
# =============================================================================
# The defect: the scan's corpus was `docker images … | grep -E '^dev-[a-z-]+:latest$'`,
# which admits no digit, so `dev-auth2:latest` was never scanned — and because
# SOME images matched, the list was non-empty and KS-676's "examined nothing"
# alarm stayed silent. The report read clean while an image was never examined.
# Partial silence, which the total-silence alarm cannot see.
#
# docker and trivy are NEVER run here (no stack, no daemon): both are STUBS on
# a private PATH that RECORD what they were asked. `docker images` prints a
# fixture list; `trivy image …` appends its last argument (the image) to a
# file and prints `{}`. Which images were scanned is read from that record —
# the one observable the job's own exit code and artefact cannot forge.
#
# Usage: bash Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/container_trivy_image_filter.test.sh
#        TRIVY_JOB_SH=/path/to/other/04-container-trivy.sh bash …   (red-proof)
# =============================================================================
set -uo pipefail

HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$HERE/../../../.." && pwd)"
# Same subject discipline as orchestrate_jobs.test.sh (KS-923 F2 / KS-941).
if [ "${TRIVY_JOB_SH+set}" = set ] && [ -z "$TRIVY_JOB_SH" ]; then
  echo "FATAL: TRIVY_JOB_SH is set but EMPTY — refusing to silently grade the shipped job." >&2
  exit 2
fi
JOB="${TRIVY_JOB_SH-$REPO_ROOT/Blockchain/Testing/jobs/04-container-trivy.sh}"
[ -f "$JOB" ] || { echo "FATAL: 04-container-trivy.sh not found at $JOB" >&2; exit 2; }
[ -r "$JOB" ] || { echo "FATAL: TRIVY_JOB_SH is not readable at $JOB" >&2; exit 2; }
command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "FATAL: jq is not on PATH — the subject cannot run, so nothing here can be graded" >&2; exit 2; }
printf 'SUBJECT %s\n        sha256 %s\n\n' "$JOB" "$(shasum -a 256 "$JOB" | cut -d" " -f1)"

WORK="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ks867.XXXXXX")"
trap 'rm -rf "$WORK"' EXIT

pass=0; fail=0
ok()  { printf '  ok   %s\n' "$1"; pass=$((pass + 1)); }
bad() { printf '  FAIL %s\n     %s\n' "$1" "$2"; fail=$((fail + 1)); }

# The fixture corpus: two lowercase-only dev tags, one DIGIT-bearing dev tag,
# and two non-dev / non-latest tags that must stay OUT whatever the class.
# Docker lower-cases repository names, so an uppercase tag cannot be produced
# and is not in this corpus — a cell that cannot be reached is not pinned.
CORPUS_DEFAULT='dev-auth:latest
dev-api-gateway:latest
dev-auth2:latest
postgres:15
dev-old:v1'
CORPUS_NONE='postgres:15
dev-old:v1'

# Build a fixture around the job under test.
#   $1 = dir   $2 = corpus text (what `docker images` prints)   $3 = up | down (docker info)
build_fixture() {
  local root="$1" corpus="$2" daemon="${3:-up}"
  rm -rf "$root"; mkdir -p "$root/Testing/jobs" "$root/bin" "$root/run"
  cp "$JOB" "$root/Testing/jobs/04-container-trivy.sh"
  printf '%s\n' "$corpus" > "$root/images.txt"
  # docker stub: `info` reports the fixture's daemon state; `images` prints the
  # corpus; every call is recorded.
  { printf '#!/bin/bash\n'
    printf 'echo "docker $*" >> "%s/docker_calls.txt"\n' "$root"
    printf 'case "${1:-}" in\n'
    if [ "$daemon" = up ]; then printf '  info) exit 0 ;;\n'; else printf '  info) exit 1 ;;\n'; fi
    printf '  images) cat "%s/images.txt" ;;\n' "$root"
    printf 'esac\nexit 0\n'
  } > "$root/bin/docker"
  # trivy stub: records the image it was asked to scan (the last argument),
  # prints an empty report.
  { printf '#!/bin/bash\n'
    printf 'for last; do :; done\n'
    printf 'echo "$last" >> "%s/trivy_scanned.txt"\n' "$root"
    printf "echo '{}'\n"
  } > "$root/bin/trivy"
  chmod +x "$root/bin/docker" "$root/bin/trivy"
}

# Run the job the way the orchestrator / audit runner do (bash, SELF + RUN_DIR
# exported), with ONLY the stub dir in front of the system dirs. Prints rc.
run_job() {
  local root="$1"
  ( export PATH="$root/bin:/usr/bin:/bin" SELF="$root/Testing" RUN_DIR="$root/run"
    cd "$SELF" && bash jobs/04-container-trivy.sh ) >"$root/out.txt" 2>&1
  echo $?
}
# `grep -c` prints its count even when it exits 1 on zero matches, so the
# `|| true` keeps the pipeline honest without printing a second 0.
scanned_times() { if [ -f "$1/trivy_scanned.txt" ]; then grep -cx -- "$2" "$1/trivy_scanned.txt" || true; else echo 0; fi; }
scanned_total() { if [ -f "$1/trivy_scanned.txt" ]; then wc -l < "$1/trivy_scanned.txt" | tr -d ' '; else echo 0; fi; }

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CELL 1 — KS-867. THE REGRESSION. A dev image whose name carries a DIGIT must
# be scanned. Measured at base: `dev-auth2:latest` scanned 0 times while the
# run printed `CRITICAL=0 HIGH=0 across 2 image(s)` and exited 0.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
build_fixture "$WORK/digit" "$CORPUS_DEFAULT"
rc_digit="$(run_job "$WORK/digit")"
if [ "$rc_digit" = 0 ] && [ "$(scanned_times "$WORK/digit" dev-auth2:latest)" -eq 1 ] \
   && [ "$(jq '.images | length' "$WORK/digit/run/04-container-trivy.json" 2>/dev/null)" = 3 ]; then
  ok "KS-867 — a digit-bearing dev image (dev-auth2:latest) IS scanned, once, and the artefact names 3 images (rc=$rc_digit)"
else
  bad "KS-867 — a digit-bearing dev image (dev-auth2:latest) is scanned" \
      "rc=$rc_digit, dev-auth2:latest scanned $(scanned_times "$WORK/digit" dev-auth2:latest) times of $(scanned_total "$WORK/digit") total, artefact images=$(jq '.images | length' "$WORK/digit/run/04-container-trivy.json" 2>/dev/null), output: $(tr '\n' ' ' < "$WORK/digit/out.txt")"
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CELL 2 — CONTROL, both directions. In the SAME run, the non-dev and non-latest
# tags must stay OUT: `postgres:15` and `dev-old:v1` scanned 0 times each, and
# the two lowercase dev tags still IN, once each. Green at base and after; a
# widened class that admitted everything would pass CELL 1 and fail here. The
# total is deliberately NOT asserted: it moves with the fix, and a control that
# moves with the fix is not a control.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
if [ "$(scanned_times "$WORK/digit" postgres:15)" -eq 0 ] && [ "$(scanned_times "$WORK/digit" dev-old:v1)" -eq 0 ] \
   && [ "$(scanned_times "$WORK/digit" dev-auth:latest)" -eq 1 ] && [ "$(scanned_times "$WORK/digit" dev-api-gateway:latest)" -eq 1 ]; then
  ok "CONTROL — postgres:15 and dev-old:v1 stay OUT (0 scans each) while the two lowercase dev tags stay IN (1 each)"
else
  bad "CONTROL — postgres:15 and dev-old:v1 stay OUT while the lowercase dev tags stay IN" \
      "scanned: $(tr '\n' ' ' < "$WORK/digit/trivy_scanned.txt" 2>/dev/null) (total $(scanned_total "$WORK/digit"))"
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CELL 3 — CONTROL (KS-676 alarm intact). A corpus with NO dev-*:latest image
# at all must still write the `no-images` error artefact and exit 1 — total
# silence stays loud after the class widens.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
build_fixture "$WORK/none" "$CORPUS_NONE"
rc_none="$(run_job "$WORK/none")"
if [ "$rc_none" = 1 ] && [ "$(jq -r '.reason' "$WORK/none/run/04-container-trivy.json" 2>/dev/null)" = no-images ] \
   && [ "$(scanned_total "$WORK/none")" -eq 0 ]; then
  ok "CONTROL — with no dev-*:latest image the job still writes reason=no-images, scans nothing, and exits 1"
else
  bad "CONTROL — with no dev-*:latest image the job still writes reason=no-images and exits 1" \
      "rc=$rc_none, reason=$(jq -r '.reason' "$WORK/none/run/04-container-trivy.json" 2>/dev/null), scans=$(scanned_total "$WORK/none")"
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CELL 4 — CONTROL (the stubs are the instrument). With the docker stub's `info`
# failing, the job must take its documented docker-unreachable SKIP: rc 0,
# reason=docker-unreachable, zero scans. Proves the job is talking to the stub
# on the private PATH and not to a real daemon — without this, every cell above
# could be describing whatever docker is on the machine.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
build_fixture "$WORK/down" "$CORPUS_DEFAULT" down
rc_down="$(run_job "$WORK/down")"
if [ "$rc_down" = 0 ] && [ "$(jq -r '.reason' "$WORK/down/run/04-container-trivy.json" 2>/dev/null)" = docker-unreachable ] \
   && [ "$(scanned_total "$WORK/down")" -eq 0 ] && grep -q '^docker info' "$WORK/down/docker_calls.txt"; then
  ok "CONTROL — the job talks to the STUB: docker info failing takes the documented docker-unreachable SKIP (rc 0, 0 scans)"
else
  bad "CONTROL — the job talks to the stub: docker info failing takes the docker-unreachable SKIP" \
      "rc=$rc_down, reason=$(jq -r '.reason' "$WORK/down/run/04-container-trivy.json" 2>/dev/null), scans=$(scanned_total "$WORK/down"), docker calls: $(tr '\n' ' ' < "$WORK/down/docker_calls.txt" 2>/dev/null)"
fi

printf '\n  %d passed, %d failed\n' "$pass" "$fail"
[ "$fail" -eq 0 ] || exit 1
exit 0
